This dual approach aims to ensure fuel availability for future reactor capacity.

While many modern SUVs have transitioned to monocoque structures, Mahindra's vehicles remain true to their engineering roots, fostering increasing demand for second-hand models in rural communities.

items.title: British fintech Revolut confirms sensitive customer data exposed in a scam; says only 'limited number' of users affected
items.summary: British fintech firm Revolut confirmed that a scam exposed sensitive customer data, including identity and contact details, documents, selfies, and transaction histories. The fintech said a limited number of customers were affected.

items.title: Russia imports record fuel from India as Ukraine strikes hit refineries
items.summary: Russia imported record oil products from India in August. This surge occurred as Ukrainian drone strikes disrupted domestic refining capacity. India supplied seventy percent of Russia's oil product imports during this period. These shipments underscore the impact of sustained Ukrainian drone campaigns. Russia's fossil-fuel export revenues saw a decline in August.

items.title: Insolvency regulator mulls tighter safeguards for personal guarantee insolvency
items.summary: India’s insolvency regulator is proposing tighter safeguards for personal guarantor cases, including zero voting rights for related-party creditors, independent asset valuations and scrutiny of questionable transactions. Creditors may also have to explain why a repayment plan offers a better outcome than bankruptcy, particularly when recoveries are low.

items.summary: Consumer group Which? has called the sale of jack mackerel, a cheaper, less nutritious species of fish, an example of "skimpflation".

items.title: PM Modi, UAE Crown Prince discuss new sovereign fund L'Imad, strategic cooperation; Malaysia ties reviewed
items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and UAE Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed discussed the role of L'Imad, the UAE's newest sovereign investment fund, in expanding bilateral ties, alongside cooperation in defence, space, nuclear energy and technology. Modi separately reviewed India-Malaysia ties with PM Anwar Ibrahim, including semiconductors, trade, defence and investment.

items.title: US determines anti dumping, countervailing duty on Indian solar cells, panels
items.summary: The US has finalized duties on solar cells and panels imported from India. Anti-dumping and countervailing duties were set for several Indian companies. Investigations into crystalline silicon photovoltaic cells are ongoing. The US International Trade Commission will determine injury to American manufacturers. This development occurs as India and the US negotiate a bilateral trade agreement.

items.title: US judge rules that Trump plan to halve FEMA workforce violated law
items.summary: A US judge ruled the Trump administration unlawfully cut FEMA's workforce. The Department of Homeland Security usurped FEMA's authority over its personnel. This action violated a federal law enacted after Hurricane Katrina. The judge found the department acted unlawfully by stopping contract renewals. Remedies and penalties for this ruling will be addressed next month.

items.title: Paying cash for Zomato orders? You may now have to pay a separate fee | All you need to know
items.summary: Zomato introduces a cash-on-delivery fee, increasing costs for customers paying in cash. The fee varies based on order value and other factors. Rivals like Swiggy do not impose similar charges, while Zomato continues to raise fees to boost its monetisation strategy amidst growing market competition.

items.title: Gem, jewellery exports rise 3.14% to $2.30 bn in August despite weak demand
items.summary: India's gem and jewellery exports grew in August, with studded gold jewellery exports surging significantly. Cut and polished diamond exports saw volume increases, though realisations remained a pressure point. Plain gold jewellery exports declined sharply due to higher gold prices and input costs. Other value-added categories like platinum and lab-grown diamonds also recorded strong growth. This trend highlights a shift towards finished and value-added jewellery in India's export profile.

items.title: BRICS leaders oppose 'punitive, discriminatory' carbon border taxes
items.summary: BRICS leaders opposed unilateral measures like carbon border adjustments. They agreed to expand cooperation on intellectual property rights and AI applications. Leaders also emphasized resilient and inclusive global value chains for trade. They will explore policy levers to enhance intra-BRICS trade and connectivity. BRICS members aim for equitable participation in global manufacturing segments.

items.title: Tehran won’t surrender to the U.S., Iranian President Pezeshkian says, as India's Modi urges dialogue and peace
items.summary: On his first visit to India, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said he will not surrender to the U.S. and Israel, as New Delhi renewed its appeal for peace.

items.title: BRICS for immediate restoration of fully functioning WTO dispute settlement system
items.summary: BRICS leaders strongly advocate for restoring the WTO dispute settlement mechanism. They committed to strengthening the organization through necessary reforms and negotiations. The Appellate Body's functioning stalled after the US blocked member appointments. Developing nations believe a two-tier system is fundamental for dispute resolution. BRICS members will engage constructively in WTO reform discussions.

items.title: BRICS leaders push faster, cheaper cross-border payments, deeper use of local currencies
items.summary: BRICS leaders are calling for faster and cheaper cross-border payments among member nations. They also support greater interoperability between national payment and messaging systems. The group encourages the BRICS Payment Task Force to continue its work on these initiatives. Iranian President Pezeshkian advocated for reduced dependence on dominant currencies. Measures were outlined to strengthen intra-BRICS trade and investment cooperation.
